data.title: Visus
data.content: Trains on your personal repository and uses NLP to offer cross insight across sources. Though the development is not transparent, this tool offers the possibility of finding new trends and insights within an artist' or researcher's own extant database.

data.title: Wonder Studio
data.content: Automates replacing actors in video footage with CGI characters, replacing mocap functions in filmmaking. This is a proprietary product with little available technical information.

data.title: Chaos Box
data.content: Uses reinforcement learning to generate NPCs, storyline and complex narrative outcomes for gameplay. Inherently interoperable with other gameworld building tools. RCT provide a more in-depth breakdown of their R&D process for the tool, with each NPC based on a uniquely trained neural network. The creative maleability of this tool is thus very high, producing indeterminate narrative outcomes.

data.title: ColossalChat
data.content: Open Source chat-interfaced LLM, built on LlamA but tuned with RLHF similar to GPT-4. This model acts as proof-of-concept that this new round of LLMs can at least in principle be open-sourced. Though its performance is hard to compare, this could be an alternative for certain chatbot usecases. Being open source it is inherently more interoperable with other tools and has a good research delineation on Github.

data.title: Prime Voice AI
data.content: Create a clone of your voice by uploading short audio samples. Offers potentially broad creative maleability and utility for artists looking to create unique generative models, however they tool's development is hard to assess as little information is provided.
